With a general strain of confidence, hope, and joy, especially in God's worship, in the midst of dangers, the Psalmist introduces prayer for divine help and guidance.</title> <div sID="gen8735" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5741"/><hi type="bold">1. light--</hi>is a common figure for comfort.<div eID="gen8735" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8736" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">strength--</hi>or, "stronghold"--affording security against all violence. entries.content_plain: PSALM 27 Psa 27:1-14 . With a general strain of confidence, hope, and joy, especially in God's worship, in the midst of dangers, the Psalmist introduces prayer for divine help and guidance. 1. light-- is a common figure for comfort. strength-- or, "stronghold"--affording security against all violence. The interrogations give greater vividness to the negation implied.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5744"/><div sID="gen8741" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5744"/>4-5. The secret of his confidence is his delight in communion with God (<reference osisRef="Ps.16.11">Psa 16:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.23.6">23:6</reference>), beholding the harmony of His perfections, and seeking His favor in His temple or palace; a term applicable to the tabernacle (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.5.7">Psa 5:7</reference>). There he is safe (<reference osisRef="Ps.31.21">Psa 31:21</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.61.5">61:5</reference>). The figure is changed in the last clause, but the sentiment is the same. <div eID="gen8741" type="x-p"/>
